What is printed by the following program?
```python
nums = [4, 2, 5, 1]
moves = 0

for i in range(1, len(nums)):
    key = nums[i]
    j = i - 1
    while j >= 0 and nums[j] > key:
        nums[j + 1] = nums[j]
        moves += 1
        j -= 1
    nums[j + 1] = key

print(moves, nums[0] + nums[-1])
```
questions.explanation: Insertion sort shifts 1, 0, and 3 items: 4 moves. Final list [1,2,4,5], first plus last = 6.

questions.text: Which actions may be appropriate when cleaning a real-world dataset?
options: B. Investigate why some values are missing.
C. Automatically replace every outlier with the mean.
D. Convert measurements to consistent units.
questions.explanation: Check duplicates and missingness; standardize units and date formats. Investigate outliers instead of automatically replacing them.

questions.text: For the dataset 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, which statements are correct?
options: D. Adding 4 to every value leaves the range unchanged.
E. Multiplying every value by 2 leaves the mean unchanged.
questions.explanation: Mean = 5; range = 8. Adding a constant preserves range. Median is 5; doubling values doubles the mean.

questions.text: Which statements about algorithms and data structures are correct?
options: A. Binary search can discard roughly half of the remaining search range after a comparison when the data is ordered.
B. A queue normally follows first-in-first-out behavior.
C. A stack removes the oldest item first.
D. The number of pairs (i, j) satisfying 0 <= i < j < n is n(n - 1)/2.
E. Linear search is always faster than binary search on a sorted list.
questions.explanation: Binary search halves ordered search ranges; queues use FIFO; there are n(n-1)/2 index pairs. Stacks use LIFO, and linear search is not always faster.

questions.text: Which statements about machine learning are correct?
options: A. Feature scaling can affect KNN because KNN uses distances.
B. K-Means is a supervised classification algorithm.
C. A decision tree can overfit its training data.
D. The sigmoid function in logistic regression can output a negative probability.
E. After the sigmoid function, logistic regression produces a value between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: Distance-based KNN is affected by scaling; trees can overfit; sigmoid outputs are between 0 and 1. K-Means is unsupervised.

questions.text:
A student is building a classifier from a dataset with missing values, duplicate records, and a
highly imbalanced target. Which practices are appropriate?
options: A. Split the data before fitting preprocessing steps such as imputation or scaling.
B. Repeatedly use the test set to choose model settings.
C. Check whether duplicate copies of the same record appear in both training and test sets.
D. Use metrics beyond accuracy when one class is much more common than the other.
E. Removing one sensitive feature always guarantees a fair model.
questions.explanation: Fit preprocessing on training data, prevent duplicate leakage, and use metrics beyond accuracy. Test-set tuning leaks information; removing a sensitive feature cannot guarantee fairness.

questions.text:


questions.text:
A KNN classifier has two features with known ranges:
0 <= x1 <= 20
0 <= x2 <= 2000
Use min-max scaling: x_scaled = (x - min) / (max - min).
The new point is P = (10, 500). The labeled points are:
A = (8, 900), Class A
B = (18, 520), Class B
C = (12, 100), Class A
D = (4, 490), Class B
(a) Scale P and the four labeled points. [3 marks]
(b) Using k = 3 and squared Euclidean distance on the scaled features, identify the three nearest
neighbors and predict the class of P. [3 marks]
(c) If the same 3-NN calculation were done on the unscaled features, what class would be
predicted? Briefly explain why the result changes. [2 marks]
questions.correctAnswer: Scaled P=(0.5,0.25); A=(0.4,0.45); B=(0.9,0.26); C=(0.6,0.05); D=(0.2,0.245). Scaled neighbors A,C,D -> Class A. Raw neighbors D,B,either A or C -> Class B.
questions.explanation: Scaling: 3 marks. Scaled squared distances A=.05, B=.1601, C=.05, D=.090025; neighbors and vote: 3 marks. Raw squared distances A=C=160004, B=464, D=136. The third-neighbor tie has the same class either way. Raw Class B and explanation of large-scale feature dominance: 2 marks.

questions.text: Which statements about Python are correct?
options: B. Dictionary keys must be unique.
C. A Python set keeps duplicate copies of the same value.
E. If b = a for a list a, appending to b can never affect a.
questions.explanation: A, B, D are true. Sets do not keep duplicates; b=a aliases the same list.

questions.text: Which actions may be appropriate when cleaning a real-world dataset?
options: B. Investigate why values are missing.
C. Replace every unusual numerical value with the mean automatically.
D. Convert measurements to consistent units.
E. Delete every row containing any outlier.
questions.explanation: Check duplicates/missingness and standardize units. Do not automatically replace or delete every unusual numerical value.

questions.text: For the dataset 2, 4, 6, 8, which statements are correct?
options: D. Adding 3 to every value leaves the range unchanged.
E. Multiplying every value by 2 leaves the mean unchanged.
questions.explanation: Mean = 5, median = 5, range = 6. Translation preserves range; doubling values doubles mean.

questions.text: Which statements about algorithms are correct?
options: A. Standard binary search requires the data to be ordered appropriately.
B. In the worst case, linear search may inspect every element.
C. Selection sort always makes exactly n^2 comparisons on n elements.
D. A queue normally follows first-in-first-out behavior.
E. A recursive solution is always faster than an iterative solution.
questions.explanation: Binary search needs ordered data; linear search may inspect all items; queues use FIFO. Standard selection sort uses n(n-1)/2 comparisons; recursion need not be faster.

questions.text: Which statements about machine learning are correct?
options: A. Feature scaling can affect KNN because KNN uses distances.
B. K-Means requires a class label for every training example.
C. A decision tree can overfit its training data.
D. 100% training accuracy guarantees 100% test accuracy.
E. Linear regression is normally used to predict numerical values.
questions.explanation: Scaling affects KNN; trees can overfit; linear regression predicts numerical values. K-Means needs no class labels, and training accuracy does not guarantee test accuracy.

questions.text:
A student is building a classifier from data containing missing values, duplicate rows, and an
imbalanced target. Which practices are appropriate?
options: A. Split into training and test sets before fitting preprocessing steps such as scaling or imputation.
B. Fit the scaler on the full dataset because scaling does not use class labels.
C. Check that duplicate copies of the same record do not appear in both training and test sets.
D. Use metrics beyond accuracy when one class is much more common than the other.
E. Repeatedly choose the model that scores highest on the test set until the score is satisfactory.
questions.explanation: Fit preprocessing after splitting; prevent duplicate leakage; inspect metrics beyond accuracy. Even label-free scaling can leak test-set information.
